security_audit.summary: All 400 presented static findings were adjudicated. Confirmed risks include remote script execution, unpinned package execution, broad credential handling, and automatic transmission or retention of project context. No prompt injection or executable obfuscation was found, but nine capped static matches remain unavailable for adjudication. Static review was capped at 400/409 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 9 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installation scripts are executed without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use a versioned package or download a pinned artifact, verify its published checksum, inspect it, and execute it as a separate step.

remediation.issue: Every CLI command automatically executes an unpinned NPM package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @insforge/cli to an audited version and update it through a reviewed release process with lockfile or integrity enforcement.

remediation.issue: Secrets are passed in command arguments or stored in predictable local files.
remediation.suggestion: Accept secrets through protected stdin or dedicated secret stores, restrict file permissions, minimize key scope, and document rotation and cleanup.

remediation.issue: Edge and compute workloads receive full project admin keys.
remediation.suggestion: Issue narrowly scoped, short-lived service credentials and prevent broad admin keys from reaching application runtimes.

remediation.issue: Feedback and durable memory can retain or transmit project context automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before each write or submission, preview the exact payload, and provide deterministic redaction and opt-out controls.

content.user_title: Manage InsForge Backends with the CLI
content.value_statement: Backend administration spans many commands and safeguards. This skill guides InsForge CLI workflows for projects, databases, deployments, integrations, and diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Creates, links, inspects, updates, and deletes InsForge projects.
Guides SQL, migrations, row-level security, integrity, import, export, and vector database workflows.
Deploys frontend applications, edge functions, container services, secrets, and scheduled jobs.
Manages branches, backups, storage, organizations, members, billing, and project configuration.
Supports Stripe, Razorpay, Apify, PostHog, AI gateway, and realtime setup.
Runs logs, health checks, advisor scans, documentation lookup, and feedback workflows.
limitations: Requires network access, an installed Node.js runtime, and access to the NPM registry.
Most cloud operations require an authenticated InsForge account and sufficient project permissions.
Destructive commands can permanently remove projects, organizations, branches, backups, storage, or local data.
Application SDK implementation belongs to the separate InsForge integration skill.

use_cases.title: Provision a Backend
use_cases.description: Create or link a project, configure services, and return verified connection details for application development.

use_cases.title: Operate Cloud Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Deploy applications and functions, manage compute services, configure schedules, and inspect production health.

use_cases.title: Govern Data and Access
use_cases.description: Plan migrations, apply row-level security, test branches, review advisor findings, and manage organization access.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the current InsForge project. Summarize its status, linked identity, and any setup required before I continue.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Database Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration for [change]. Include grants, row-level security, integrity checks, and a safe verification plan.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy an Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare and deploy [application path] to InsForge. Verify environment variables, run a local build, deploy, and report the resulting status.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [production change]. Use an isolated branch when needed, define rollback steps, request approval for destructive actions, and verify logs and advisor results.

output_examples.input: Check whether my linked project is ready for a database migration.
output_examples.output: Project status: ready. Authentication and project linkage are valid. Review the pending migration, confirm the target branch, then apply and verify it.

output_examples.input: Deploy my frontend and confirm its environment settings.
output_examples.output: The local build passed. Required public connection variables are configured, excluded secret files were not uploaded, and the deployment reached a healthy state.

output_examples.input: Review a destructive branch reset before running it.
output_examples.output: The reset restores the branch database to its original snapshot and removes later data changes. Confirm the branch name and preserve needed data first.

best_practices: Confirm the active project, organization, and branch before any write or deployment.
Keep administrative keys server-only and use protected secret handling instead of inline command arguments.
Use branches, dry runs, backups, and explicit approval before destructive or billing-impacting operations.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass CLI safeguards with undocumented backend requests.
Do not expose admin keys through public environment variables, logs, source control, or frontend bundles.
Do not auto-approve deletion, reset, transfer, role, or billing changes without clear user confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages InsForge projects, databases, deployments, functions, compute, schedules, integrations, diagnostics, billing, organizations, and related CLI workflows.

faq.question: Does it write application code using the InsForge SDK?
faq.answer: No. Use the separate InsForge application integration skill for frontend, backend, or edge code that calls the SDK.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Cloud operations usually require authentication. Self-hosted local operations can work without platform login after the project is linked.

faq.question: Can it run destructive commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Some commands delete data or infrastructure, so the skill requires explicit confirmation and target verification.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Keep full-access keys server-only, avoid public prefixes, use protected secret stores, and never place live secrets in logs or source control.

faq.question: Can it manage local InsForge instances?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user explicitly requests Docker-based local infrastructure. The first setup requires network access and downloads runtime components.
